title: Soft Third
aim: Land your third shot soft in the kitchen after a real serve and return, and know when to drop and when to drive instead.

stages.title: Fifteen Soft Drops
stages.inShort: B plays balls like a return, and A answers each one from the baseline with a soft drop into the kitchen. 15 balls, then swap.
rules: A stands behind the baseline. B stands at the kitchen line on the other side and starts every ball: a flat, medium-deep ball, like a return.
B mixes where the balls go: to A's forehand, backhand and middle, in a set order (for example forehand, backhand, forehand).
A moves the feet to the ball and lets it rise and fall: hit it on the way down, after its highest point.
A plays a drop (a soft ball that lands in the kitchen), cross-court or to the middle: about 45 cm over the net, landing in the kitchen close to B's feet.
After each ball, A notes silently: good, too high, or into the net. B says nothing.
stages.tooEasy: B plays the balls at real return pace, and after each drop A moves forward and split-steps (a small hop that lands just as B hits).
stages.tooHard: B plays slow, medium balls, always to the same spot.
stages.goodLooksLike: About 12 of 15 drops are good: low over the net and landing in the kitchen.

stages.title: Three Balls, One Point
stages.inShort: A serves deep, B returns deep, A drops into the kitchen. A point counts only when all three balls land right.
rules: Mark a strip about 1.2 m deep in front of each baseline, with a shoe or bottle on each sideline. That is the target for serve and return.
A serves deep into B's strip. B returns deep into A's strip. A plays the third shot as a drop (a soft ball that lands in the kitchen).
A point counts only when all three land right: serve in the strip, return in the strip, drop in the kitchen.
Give the third shot equal time cross-court and straight ahead, because real thirds come from both.
stages.tooEasy: Keep playing after the third shot: play the point out. Still easy: make the strips narrower.
stages.tooHard: Play cooperatively at low pace, and only think about getting the serve and return deep.
stages.goodLooksLike: A plays the drop from wherever the return really lands, not from a standing start.

stages.title: Drive or Drop
stages.inShort: A starts at the baseline, chooses drive or drop by the ball, then plays the point out. A needs 7 points, B needs 11.
rules: A stands behind the baseline, B at the kitchen line. B starts every rally with an easy, deep ball to A.
A plays a drive (a hard, low shot) and a drop as a combination, choosing by the ball: well balanced and the ball in front of you = drive; stretched, short or off balance = drop.
After the combination, the point is live: play it out.
Both score on every rally. A needs 7, B needs 11, because A starts from the baseline. Then swap roles.
After a rally, B may say whether A's choice fit the ball.
stages.tooEasy: After every good drop, B attacks actively instead of playing it back.
stages.tooHard: No score. B blocks every ball back easily, and A simply alternates drive, drop, drive, drop. Still too hard: practise only the forehand side, then only the backhand side.
stages.goodLooksLike: A drives only a ball in front of the body and drops when stretched or late. The choice comes from the ball, not from a plan.

drill.title: Drive–Drop Combo with Role Switch (7-11 Format)

goal.label: Make our third shot land soft
